sourceNote: Static offline reference using official JR East, Tokyo Metro and Toei Transportation line/station information. Not live service data. Landmark names and areas were expanded using official city tourism resources; station links are a static orientation aid, not live journey planning.
notice: Offline orientation guide only. Train types, through-services, platform assignments, delays and temporary service changes can vary. Always follow current station signs and operator announcements.

lines.name: Yamanote Line
lines.directionForward: Inner Loop (内回り) · toward Ueno / Tokyo from the west side
lines.directionReverse: Outer Loop (外回り) · toward Shibuya / Shinagawa from the east side
lines.summary: Tokyo's famous JR loop linking Shinjuku, Shibuya, Shinagawa, Tokyo, Ueno and Ikebukuro.

lines.name: Chuo Line (Rapid) · Tokyo Core
lines.summary: Fast east-west JR corridor from Tokyo through Shinjuku toward Kichijoji and Mitaka.
lines.serviceNote: This guide shows station order. Rapid stopping patterns can vary by train and day.

lines.name: Keihin-Tohoku Line · Tokyo–Yokohama Core
lines.summary: Useful north-south JR corridor sharing many central Tokyo stations before continuing to Kawasaki and Yokohama.
lines.serviceNote: Some daytime services operate as Rapid through central Tokyo. Always check the train display.

lines.name: Ginza Line
lines.summary: A central Tokyo subway line linking Shibuya, Ginza, Ueno and Asakusa.
